summary.text: A 67-year-old man with persistent atrial fibrillation lasting 4 months and obesity, with congestive heart failure, hypertension and diabetes mellitus listed among his CHADS2 components, was admitted for catheter ablation. He had no history of respiratory disease. General anesthesia used propofol, fentanyl and dexmedetomidine without a prophylactic neuromuscular blocking agent, and a size 5 i-gel laryngeal mask airway was inserted on the first attempt.

Immediately after the first pulsed field ablation application to the left superior pulmonary vein he had a forceful cough, complete loss of the capnographic waveform, hypoventilation and SpO2 of 84%. Laryngeal mask repositioning, bag-valve-mask ventilation and suctioning were ineffective; a 50 mg propofol bolus led to gradual recovery within 3 minutes. Hypoventilation from increased airway resistance recurred despite deeper anesthesia, with brief minor desaturations that resolved within 30 seconds.

Pulmonary vein isolation was completed with 36 pulsed field ablation applications over 135 minutes. Emergence from anesthesia was uneventful and no postoperative neurological or respiratory complications were noted. Laryngospasm was suspected but not directly confirmed by fiberoptic visualization.

summary.text: A 68-year-old woman with hypertension listed among her CHADS2 components, who had radiofrequency ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation 4 years earlier, presented with recurrence and underwent pulsed field ablation. She had no history of respiratory disease. A size 4 i-gel laryngeal mask airway was inserted uneventfully without a prophylactic neuromuscular blocking agent, and ventilation was adequate until ablation began.

Reconnection of the left superior and left inferior pulmonary veins was observed. Immediately after ablation at the left superior pulmonary vein she had violent coughing, complete ventilatory failure, capnogram disappearance, SpO2 of 81% and absent breath sounds. Repositioning and bag-valve-mask ventilation were unsuccessful; intravenous rocuronium 50 mg restored ventilation within 3 minutes, with a train-of-four count of 0/4 and no further episodes.

The left pulmonary veins and left atrial posterior wall were reisolated with 25 applications over 145 minutes. Sugammadex 200 mg was given after the procedure to antagonize rocuronium. Emergence and extubation were uneventful and no postoperative neurological or respiratory complications were observed.

summary.text: A 52-year-old man with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation for over 3 years, obesity and hypertension listed among his CHADS2 components underwent pulsed field ablation. He had no history of respiratory disease. A size 5 i-gel laryngeal mask airway was inserted without difficulty, ventilation was adequate, and electroanatomic mapping used an HD Grid catheter. Rocuronium 70 mg was given 5 minutes before the first application, with a train-of-four count of 0/4.

Approximately 40 minutes later, with presumed neuromuscular recovery (TOF count 4/4), complete ventilatory failure occurred immediately after ablation at the left inferior pulmonary vein antrum, with BIS 37, SpO2 78% and absent breathing sounds. Repositioning and manual ventilation were ineffective; an additional rocuronium 50 mg achieved a TOF count of 0/4 and restored ventilation within 2 minutes, with full recovery by 3 minutes and no further episodes.

A total of 37 applications were delivered over 148 minutes. Rocuronium was reversed with sugammadex 400 mg after the procedure. Emergence and extubation were uneventful and no postoperative neurological or respiratory complications were observed.
